page: Vultr vcg-a40-4c-20g-8vram is a fractional GPU instance within the Cloud GPU family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs consisting of 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 20.0 GB of system memory. The GPU component consists of a fractional slice of 0.1667 of an NVIDIA Ampere A40 GPU, providing 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is provided by a 360 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data shows strong performance in specific workloads, particularly LLM inference. For a small 135M model, prompt processing reaches 9881.81 tokens per second and text generation reaches 465.27 tokens per second, both placing in the top tier. Similarly, for a medium 7B model, prompt processing achieves 3161.22 tokens per second and text generation reaches 107.91 tokens per second. General CPU performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1384.0 and a multi-core score of 4549.0. However, some areas show weaker performance, such as Passmark database operations at 1916.13 and static web serving throughput at 5.81 GB per second.

This instance offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads by utilizing a fractional GPU slice rather than a full dedicated card, making it highly resource-dense for smaller-scale deployments. It is well-suited for light LLM inference, small-scale machine learning model development, and GPU-accelerated rendering or image processing tasks. It is less optimal for heavy database operations or high-throughput static web serving due to the observed benchmark bottlenecks in those areas.
